title: nCHANT #01
subtitle: On Digital Gardens
abstract: nCHANT is REINCANTAMENTO’s monographic magazine — an oblique optical device for exploring unusual ideas, a polyphonic, anti-disciplinary chorus of voices examining concepts at the membrane between culture and technology.
intro: nCHANT is REINCANTAMENTO’s monographic magazine — an oblique optical device for exploring unusual ideas, a polyphonic, anti-disciplinary chorus of voices examining concepts at the membrane between culture and technology.

The inaugural issue, titled “On Digital Gardens”, examines symbolic spaces that embody the desire for a post-capitalist Internet. Digital gardens are realms for autonomous knowledge organization and self-expression, elements that commercial platforms continue to short-circuit. They function as fields of seeded ideas and unfinished thoughts, waiting for their time to flourish, die, and be born again — a wilder, more personal Web waiting to be rediscovered.
sections: The 92-page publication includes a research report based on 20+ practitioner interviews from the Trust community in Berlin; essays on fractal software structures; practical self-hosting guides; a philosophical dialogue on desire; and spatial garden analyses.
Dimensions 176 × 250 mm. 92 pages. ISSN 3052-1556. Design by Giorgio Craparo, printed by SkillPress, Venice. Funded by the Trust Community.

title: Arcane Affinities
subtitle: Esoteric Algorithms & Re-Enchanted Technologies
abstract: Arcane Affinities brings together two international exhibitions, gathering artworks and essays that explore how esoteric practices can reactivate agency and technological imagination.
intro: Arcane Affinities brings together two international exhibitions, gathering artworks and essays that explore how esoteric practices can reactivate agency and technological imagination.

It functions as a catalogue connecting two exhibitions — Esoteric Algorithms and Re-Enchanted Technologies at Panke Gallery (Berlin) and Esoteric Ecotechnics at MFRU 25 (Maribor). The publication assembles artworks, essays and experimental methods investigating how hermetic thinking can restore agency.
credits: Linz-based platform for net culture and critical digital practice
sections: Dimensions 170 × 240 mm. 68 pages, staple binding. ISBN 978-3-9504200-4-3. Graphic design by Giorgio Craparo, printed by SkillPress, Venice, Italy. Co-published with servus.at.
